svg.title: Portugal wine-growing study atlas
svg.desc: Follow mainland Portugal from the Atlantic northwest to the warmer south, then locate Madeira separately in the Atlantic. Approximate study locations, not appellation boundaries. Numbers refer to the study key; a shared number connects places in one grouped lesson. 1: Vinho Verde. Northwestern Portugal, north of Porto; the locator stands for a broad, varied region. 2: Douro / Port. The inland Douro valley east of Porto. Port’s vineyard origin and the coastal trade centers should not be conflated. 3: Dão. Inland central-northern Portugal, south of the Douro. 4: Bairrada. West of Dão and closer to the Atlantic. 5: Lisboa. Atlantic-influenced wine country north of Lisbon. 6: Tejo. The Tagus corridor northeast of Lisbon. 7: Setúbal. The peninsula southeast of Lisbon, across the Tagus estuary. 8: Alentejo. A broad inland region east and southeast of Lisbon. 9: Madeira. Atlantic island southwest of mainland Portugal and west of Morocco; displayed in a separately scaled inset.

g.text: Dots locate representative places · boundaries do not represent appellations
